newsitem.title: USA: Cargo at Boston airport up 11.4% in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cargo at Boston airport up 11.4% in Q1 1997.

text.p: Logan International Airport handled 11.4 percent more cargo in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the first three months of 1996, the airport authority said.
This marked the first time in over three years that Logan's cargo volumes maintained double digit growth during an entire quarter, Massport said in a statement.
Between January and March, Logan handled 189.9 million pounds of air cargo, excluding mail.
Domestic cargo totalled 146.5 million pounds, a 10 percent increase.
International cargo was 43.3 million points, up 14 percent over the same three months of 1996.
Computer and electronic equipment, medical devices and instruments and seafood are among the top commodities exported from New England's largest airport, Massport said.

"We added our first direct Asian carrier with Korean Airlines service to Seoul beginning last August, and service to Lisbon and the Azores with TAP last December," said Massport executive director Peter Blute.

Blute said the airport has outreach programs to encourage small and medium-sized businesses to explore foreign markets by participating in foreign trade shows, forming joint partnerships or contracting with foreign distributors. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
